pageCache.text:
Inspiring hearts and minds
School places available. Places are currently available in Year 3, Year 4 and Year 6. Contact the school office to find out more.
Welcome to Shellingford CE (A) Primary School
Welcome to our school community. Whether you are a current family, a prospective parent or a visitor, we hope our website gives you a clear sense of who we are and what makes Shellingford such a special place to learn and grow.
We are proud to be judged Good by Ofsted and recognised by SIAMS as a school that is living up to its foundation as a Church school and enabling both pupils and adults to flourish.
Our motto, Inspiring hearts and minds, sits at the centre of school life. Rooted in our Christian vision to build ‘roots and foundations in love’ (Ephesians 3:17–18), we nurture curiosity, compassion and confidence in every child.
We are proud of our school community and warmly welcome visits from prospective families. If you would like to learn more about Shellingford, we would be delighted to show you around.
Headteacher Welcome
At Shellingford CE (A) Primary School we are proud to be a small village school where every child is known, valued and encouraged to flourish. Our close-knit community creates a nurturing environment where children feel confident to explore new ideas, build friendships and develop a lifelong love of learning.
I feel incredibly proud to lead such a caring and dedicated school community and look forward to welcoming you to Shellingford.
Miss Judith TerrellHeadteacher
SIAMS inspection
Our most recent SIAMS inspection took place on 4 March 2025. The report recognises that our Church of England foundation is central to school life and that our Christian vision and values guide every decision we make for pupils and adults.
Ofsted inspection
Our most recent Ofsted inspection took place on 8 June 2022.
The school was judged to be Good overall.
Join our schoolcommunity
We warmly welcome visits from prospective families. Contact the school office to arrange a tour or find out more about places available.

pageCache.text:
PE and Sports Premium
Shellingford CE (A) Primary School receives PE and Sports Premium funding from the government to enhance the quality of physical education, sport and physical activity within the school.
This funding helps us improve sports provision, develop staff expertise and encourage pupils to lead active and healthy lifestyles.
Details of how this funding is used and the impact it has on pupils can be found in the documents below.

Enrichment and Experiences | Explore Enriching Learning Opportunities — Shellingford CE (A) Primary School
pageCache.text:
Enrichment and Experiences
At Shellingford CE (A) Primary School, we believe that learning extends beyond the classroom. Alongside a strong academic curriculum, we provide a wide range of experiences that help children develop confidence, curiosity and independence.
Through visits, visitors, clubs and community partnerships, pupils have opportunities to explore new interests, build important life skills and create lasting memories throughout their time at school.
Learning Beyond the Classroom
Pupils take part in a wide range of activities that enrich their learning and help bring the curriculum to life.
We enjoy strong links with other local schools in the partnership and regularly take part in shared events such as music festivals, engineering days, sporting competitions and Junior Citizens programmes.
Educational visits are an important part of school life. Recent trips have included Coleshill House WWII Auxiliary Unit, The Tate Modern in London, The Steam Museum of the Great Western Railway in Swindon, the Sheldonian Winter Concert in Oxford and the Watermill Theatre in Newbury.
Each year, our oldest pupils take part in an exciting five-day residential visit to Yenworthy Lodge on the North Devon coast, where they develop independence, teamwork and confidence.
Our oldest children also attend weekly swimming sessions for one term, helping them build important life skills and water confidence.
Visitors regularly work alongside the school to deliver curriculum workshops. Recent experiences have included African drumming, felt-making with a visiting artist, and tennis coaching.
We also invite parents and members of the local community to share their expertise with pupils, helping to inspire curiosity and broaden children’s learning experiences.
Clubs and Activities
A range of after-school clubs are offered throughout the year, giving pupils opportunities to explore new interests, develop skills and enjoy activities with friends beyond the school day.
Clubs vary from term to term and may include activities such as sport, music, arts and crafts, science, languages and technology. Many clubs are run by staff, specialist providers or external organisations working alongside the school.
Places in clubs may be limited and some activities may carry a small charge depending on the provider.
View the current after-school clubs and timetable below.
Registration and booking for all clubs is managed through School Gateway, where parents can view availability and sign their child up to participate.
Our Year 5 pupils also play an active role in school life as Junior Active Leaders, organising and leading a variety of playground activities to support younger children during lunchtime.
School and Home Partnership
We value the strong partnership between school and home and believe that children learn best when families and staff work closely together.
Parents and carers are encouraged to take an active role in their child’s education. We support this partnership through parent–teacher meetings, curriculum information sessions, workshops, home–school communication and weekly Celebration Assemblies, where pupils’ achievements are shared and celebrated.
Teachers also provide pupil next steps to help guide parents in supporting learning at home and to encourage children to continue developing their skills and confidence.
All pupils receive an appropriate level of homework, which may include a range of activities that reinforce and extend learning from school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Reading and Phonics | Explore Our Reading & Phonics Curriculum — Shellingford CE (A) Primary School
pageCache.text:
Reading and Phonics
At Shellingford CE (A) Primary School, we believe that learning to read is one of the most important skills children develop during their time at school. Reading opens the door to learning across the curriculum and helps children build confidence, imagination and independence.
Our approach combines systematic phonics teaching with a strong culture of reading for pleasure, helping every child develop the skills and enthusiasm they need to become confident readers.
Reading at Home
Phonics also supports children’s writing. As they learn to recognise and use different sounds, pupils become more confident in spelling and word building.
Children are also taught letter formation and handwriting to support the development of fluent writing.
Learning to Read Through Phonics
Children begin learning phonics as soon as they start in the Early Years, with daily phonics sessions in Reception and Key Stage 1. At Shellingford CE (A) Primary School we use the DfE-validated Twinkl Phonics scheme to support early reading and writing.
Through phonics teaching, children learn to:
recognise the sounds that letters represent
blend sounds together to read words
segment sounds to help with spelling
apply these skills when reading and writing independently
Phonics continues throughout Key Stage 1 and is revisited in Key Stage 2 where additional support may be needed to consolidate early reading skills.
Developing Confident Readers
Alongside phonics teaching, we encourage all pupils to develop a genuine enjoyment of books and stories. Children regularly share books in class, explore a range of texts and are encouraged to read widely both in school and at home.
Our aim is for every child to become a fluent reader who not only reads with confidence but also develops a lasting love of literature.
Resources for Parents
Parents can find helpful resources in the Parents section of the website.

pageCache.pageTitle: SEND | Discover Inclusive Support Opportunities — Shellingford CE (A) Primary School
pageCache.text:
Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND)
Shellingford CE (A) Primary School is an inclusive school where every pupil is valued as a member of our community. We aim to ensure that all children receive the support they need to make the best possible progress educationally, socially and emotionally.
SEND Team
Miss Katie Long – SENCo
01367 710301office.3853@shellingford.oxon.sch.uk
Further information about SEND provision at Shellingford CE (A) Primary School can be found in the sections below.
Our Approach to SEND
All pupils, regardless of their needs, are offered teaching and learning experiences that enable them to participate fully in school life.
Support may include:
high quality teaching that is carefully differentiated to meet individual needs
access to individual or small group intervention programmes
multi-sensory resources and learning approaches
personalised programmes designed to support specific pupils
the use of technology and software to promote independence in learning
physical adaptations to ensure access to school buildings and grounds
Further information about how we support pupils with SEND can be found in our SEND Policy.
What is Special Educational Needs?
Special Educational Needs (SEN) refers to a learning difficulty or disability that requires provision that is additional to, or different from, the support normally provided in the classroom.
communication and interaction
cognition and learning
social, emotional and mental health
sensory or physical needs
Some needs may be short-term, while others may require longer-term support throughout a child’s time at school.
Specialist Support
Within the school we have a dedicated SEND team:
Miss Katie Long – SENCoMiss Jo Harris – Assistant SENCo
We also work closely with a range of external professionals and services when appropriate, including:
Educational Psychologists
Special Educational Needs Support Service (SENSS)
Speech and Language Therapy
Occupational Therapy
These services help us ensure that pupils receive the most appropriate support.
Monitoring Progress
Progress for pupils with SEND is regularly reviewed through:
Pupil Profiles used by teachers to track provision and progress
SEND consultations with parents, teachers and the SENCo
Annual reviews for pupils with Education, Health and Care (EHC) plans
Further details can be found in the SEND Policy.
Transition to Secondary School
Moving to a new school is an important step for every pupil. We work carefully to support pupils with SEND during transition to secondary school.
Support may include:
additional transition visits
small group or individual preparation sessions
transition books using photographs and information about the new school
communication with staff at the receiving school
This support is tailored to meet the needs of each individual pupil.

pageCache.pageTitle: Curriculum | Explore Our Curriculum—Learn More Today — Shellingford CE (A) Primary School
pageCache.text:
Curriculum
At Shellingford CE (A) Primary School, our curriculum inspires curiosity, builds confidence and encourages a lifelong love of learning. Guided by our vision of Inspiring hearts and minds, we nurture children who are creative, thoughtful and independent learners.
Rooted in our Christian ethos of building ‘roots and foundations in love’ (Ephesians 3:17–18), pupils develop knowledge, skills and understanding while also growing in character, resilience and respect for others.
Religious Education plays an important role in school life, helping children explore faith, values and beliefs while developing understanding and respect for people of all backgrounds.
Teaching
We provide children with a wide range of learning opportunities delivered by skilled and experienced staff. Our aim is to help every child develop the knowledge, skills and understanding they need to become confident and independent learners.
Children are placed at the centre of their learning. Lessons are designed to be meaningful and engaging, encouraging pupils to ask questions, think creatively and explore ideas in depth.
Where possible, subjects are linked through topic-based learning, allowing children to make connections across different areas of the curriculum. Topics have included themes such as Inventions and Invaders, Tales from Other Lands, Performance and Theatre, and Our Locality.
We are also fortunate to make full use of our outdoor environment, which provides opportunities for practical learning, physical activity and exploration of environmental issues.
Assessment
Assessment is an important part of teaching and learning. Teachers continually assess pupils’ understanding through discussion, observation and the evaluation of work in the classroom.
These ongoing assessments help teachers adapt lessons to meet children’s needs. More formal assessments may also take place at key points during the year to monitor progress and support each child’s development.
Learning Culture
At Shellingford we promote a positive learning culture, encouraging children to develop a growth mindset and to see challenges as opportunities to learn.
We support pupils in developing the language of learning so that they can understand their strengths and identify areas for improvement. By involving children in reflecting on their learning, we help them build confidence, independence and strong problem-solving skills.
Specialist Learning
Throughout the week, teachers are given dedicated time to plan and review pupils’ learning. During these sessions, children benefit from specialist teaching in subjects such as physical education, art and music.
We also draw on staff expertise across the school to provide additional learning opportunities, including Forest School activities, languages and computing.
Curriculum Information
You can find detailed information about what pupils learn in each stage of the school in the documents below. Parents may request further information about the curriculum by contacting the school office.

pageCache.pageTitle: Mathematics | Explore Our Maths Curriculum — Shellingford CE (A) Primary School
pageCache.text:
Mathematics
At Shellingford CE (A) Primary School, we aim to develop confident and capable mathematicians who enjoy solving problems and exploring new ideas. Mathematics is taught through a balance of fluency, reasoning and problem-solving, helping children build secure understanding as they progress through the school.
Through engaging lessons and practical activities, pupils develop the skills and confidence needed to apply mathematics in a range of contexts.
How Mathematics is Taught
Our maths curriculum supports pupils in developing strong number sense and a deep understanding of mathematical concepts. Lessons encourage children to explain their thinking, explore different strategies and apply their learning to real-life problems.
Teachers provide opportunities for pupils to work both independently and collaboratively, helping them build confidence and resilience when tackling new challenges.
Building Mathematical Confidence
Children are encouraged to:
develop fluency in key mathematical skills
reason and explain their thinking
solve problems using a range of strategies
apply mathematics across the wider curriculum
This approach helps pupils become confident learners who can use mathematics in everyday situations.
Supporting Learning at Home
To support consistency in teaching and learning, the school uses a clear progression of calculation strategies. These show how mathematical methods develop as pupils move through the school.

Our People
At Shellingford CE (A) Primary School, our strength lies in our people. Together, staff, governors and pupils work in partnership to create a nurturing, ambitious and values-led community where every child can flourish.
We are proud of the dedication, experience and care shown by everyone involved in school life.
Senior Leadership and Teaching Staff
Our teaching team is committed to delivering high quality education within a supportive and inclusive environment. Every member of staff plays an important role in inspiring hearts and minds. Each teacher brings expertise, creativity and enthusiasm to the classroom, ensuring children are both challenged and supported in their learning.
